title: Healthy eating
intro: Eat and drink, but do not overdo it – food is for health and strength to worship Allah.

learn.title: 📖 In the Qur’an
learn.html: Eat and drink, but do not be excessive – Allah does not love those who are excessive. <small>(Qur’an, Al-A‘raf 7:31)</small>

Allah created people and gave them countless blessings. Among the most important are food, water and air – and also health. To look after the blessing of health, we must first of all eat healthily: varied, good and tasty food that Allah has allowed, with everything the body needs – milk and dairy, honey, grains, fruit and vegetables, and meat.

Islam teaches that eating too much is forbidden and harmful: it damages health and causes many problems. Today many people suffer from obesity, a direct result of overeating. Unhealthy food causes many illnesses, so a Muslim protects their health by eating halal food in moderation.
These are some of the foods mentioned in the Qur’an. Others are onions, cucumbers, bananas and squash.

items: pork, pork fat and anything made from pork
meat of animals that died by themselves
meat of predators, reptiles and rodents
overeating any food – even halal food

learn.title: ⭐ Remember
learn.html: A Muslim sees food as a way to keep life and health, to have strength to worship Allah and live well. So a Muslim does not eat until hungry and does not drink until thirsty. The Prophet (SAW) said: “A person fills no vessel worse than his stomach…” (Ahmad)

questions.q: What does Allah say in Al-A‘raf 7:31?
options: Eat and drink, but do not be excessive
Eat as much as you can
To keep life and health and have strength to worship

questions.q: Is it allowed to eat too much halal food?
options: No – overeating is forbidden and harmful

questions.q: What did the Prophet (SAW) say is the worst vessel to fill?

practice.title: Talk and tasks
prompts: 💬 When and why does a Muslim eat and drink?

📋 Make a table: “I eat sweets and fast food”, “I eat dairy”, “I check the ingredients”, “I drink fizzy drinks” – always, often, sometimes or never. Compare with a friend: who looks after their health better?
